messages:
Ada: Quick design review — attached mocks for the min/max control inside the compact pool picker. Goal: reduce cognitive load when switching pools + editing min/max/burst. Thoughts?

Sam: Quick notes: the compact layout hides the stepper for min. People try to drag the bar; we need an affordance. :thinking:

Jess: Agree. Maybe show a subtle drag handle and keep steppers visible on focus. Also the min/max labels should include units (GPUs). Right now it's ambiguous.

Mike: Copy nit: "Min" / "Max" feels terse. Suggest "Min instances" / "Max instances" or "Min GPUs" / "Max GPUs" depending on unit. Leaning to "GPUs" to avoid confusion with nodes.

Olivia: Accessibility: keyboard flow breaks when switching pools — tabbing from pool select lands inside the SLO slider and skips the burst knob. We should enforce a logical order: pool -> min -> max -> burst -> SLO slider -> save.

Ada: Design question — do we show cost delta inline as the user adjusts sliders? Concern about flicker and noise when people are fiddling with SLOs.

Sam: I'd like an inline "estimated cost / hr" that updates on debounce (250ms). Visual weight should be light (muted text) but persistent so users can see immediate impact.

Jess: Regarding guardrails: when user sets Min > Max (edge case), show an inline validation message and suggest a small "swap values" CTA + brief tooltip explaining autoscale behavior. Also add an inline hint for burst: "Burst is temporary capacity; it won't change your reserved commit."

Mike: Microcopy for SLO slider: current "SLO" label isn't clear. Suggest "Latency SLO (p95 ms)" with a tooltip that says "Target p95 latency for this pool; lower is faster but costlier."

Olivia: For screen readers, use aria-live on the cost preview so SRs announce the new estimate. Also aria-label the burst toggle: aria-label="Enable burst capacity".

Ada: UX trade: compactness vs discoverability. If we keep everything compact, new users miss the burst knob. Maybe collapse advanced controls under "More options" but default to expanded for power users who used the pool recently. Persist preference in local storage.

Sam: Implementation note: prefer using role="slider" for SLO with proper keyboard support. Add aria-valuetext like `aria-valuetext="Target p95 200 ms"` so screen readers say human-friendly values.

Jess: Action items: mock revisions with (1) clearer unit copy, (2) focus order fix, (3) cost debounce, (4) inline validation when Min>Max, (5) collapsible advanced with persisted preference. I'll update mocks and post in #design when ready.

Ada: Awesome, thanks. @Jess please tag eng when you post so we can triage complexity. :thumbsup:

DesignBot: Mock uploaded — https://redwood.design/mock/2185012345 (added to thread).

Sam: One tiny thought — show a small "recommended" badge on SLO presets (e.g., "Balanced") so people have a quick safe pick.

Mike: SGTM. We should also log a metric when users change Min/Max frequently; that could indicate confusion and be useful for iterating the affordances.

Jess: Will include a quick analytics spike: track rapid min/max toggles, number of times swap CTA is used, and how often cost preview is dismissed.

Ada: Cool — let's reconvene after the mock update. Thanks all!
